key_insight: The paper turns disruption response in supply chains into an open capacity pooling problem, where ADMM coordinates incumbents and an LLM-guided search helps discover outside capacity offers without sharing private models.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical framework for resilient supply-chain re-optimization under capacity shortages, combining privacy-preserving coordination with automated provider discovery and screening.
method: Use ADMM to coordinate incumbent supply-chain decisions without exposing full models.
Search provider profiles with an LLM to rank likely compatible capacity offers from residual gaps.
Verify offers, screen by reduced cost, then warm-start ADMM for re-optimization.
evidence_signal: Across 200 synthetic episodes, full-information opening recovered 24.6% of capacity-scarcity cost, while 40-contact coordination-directed LLM search captured 32.0% of that value versus 4.7% for undirected contact.
watch_item: The approach is only optimal when every eligible offer is revealed at exact prices; performance is heuristic when offer disclosure is incomplete or profiles omit key capacity details.
paper_title: Open Capacity Pooling in Agentic Supply Chains: Coordination-Directed LLM Discovery and Distributed Re-optimization
